newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Samsung mulls further chip output cut.
newsitem.headline: Samsung mulls further chip output cut.

text.p: Samsung Electronics Co, the world's leading chipmaker, may have to cut production of memory chips by 20 to 30 percent this year because of low prices, a company spokesman said.
Samsung Electronics, flagship of South Korea's Samsung Group random access memory (DRAM) chips from the fourth quarter of 1996 but their prices remained below production costs, the spokesman said.
"We may have to cut memory production by 20 to 30 percent this year. If the price does not rise to cover costs after that, a further reduction might be inevitable," he said.
Industry analysts said spot price for 16 megabit DRAM chips now hovered at around $8, up from about $6 a month ago, but down sharply from about $40 to $50 a year ago.
The spokesman said the percentage of the cut would be based on last year's volume but he declined to give any output figure.
"We believe the optimal price to cover costs would be around $10-$12," he said.

Samsung said it would use extra production capacity after cutting 16 megabit output to make other higher-value memory chips, such as graphic memories, and non-memory chips, including application-specific integrated circuits (ASICs).
